This is PR #81 in ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa, "feat(pdp): SFCC-731 product gallery + full-bleed hero layout" by Tim Lavelle. It has already been through ~9 rounds of local CodeRabbit fixes; your job is to independently find what's still wrong, not restate what's already fixed.

WORKTREES (already checked out, dependencies installed — use these, do not re-clone):
- Head (review this): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/37973080-8be5-46e1-9aab-e2abcb81ea17/scratchpad/pr81-head  (commit 6284ea3511305524156489a6c0e811a85bb2a17a)

GATE NUMBERS — ALREADY MEASURED BY ME. DO NOT RE-RUN tsc/lint/vitest/audit:tokens; spend your budget on what these can't see:
- tsc --noEmit: clean on both head and base.
- lint: base 5 errors/21 warnings → head 4 errors/21 warnings. All 4 head errors are pre-existing (useHeaderNav.test.ts:106, productInfo.test.ts:9/209/236 — files this PR doesn't touch). Net PR-introduced lint errors: zero (the PR actually fixes one pre-existing prettier error in product-view/index.tsx as a side effect of rewriting that region).
- audit:tokens (scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs): base 2 unacknowledged violations (footer.css.ts:20, zimmDrawerShared.ts:12 — untouched by this PR) → head same 2, unchanged. Zero new unacknowledged violations. The PR does add several NEW raw px/rem values in touched/new files (product-view/index.tsx 218px content-column width x2, zimmColourSwatch.css.ts 47px/72px, zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts 45rem/6.375rem, zimmButton.css.ts's pre-existing 50px/41px/5px) but all fall in the script's "acknowledged exception" bucket (meaning they already carry a provisional/pending/placeholder comment) — confirm this is actually true by reading the comments at those exact lines yourself, don't just trust the bucket.
- vitest: base 695/695 passing (46 files). Head 768/768 passing (52 files) — I confirmed this myself: a full-suite run showed 1 failure (zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx "ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move focus between thumbnails, wrapping at each end" timed out at 5000ms), but re-running that exact test in isolation 3x in the head worktree passed all 3 times (with a benign "Could not parse CSS stylesheet" jsdom stderr warning each time, unrelated). Classify this as environment/worker-contention flake under full-suite parallel load, not a PR defect — CI's own Vitest job on this PR also went green. Do not re-flag this as a new finding unless you find a concrete reason (e.g. a real race condition in the component's own focus-management code) it should behave differently — if you do find such a reason, that IS worth reporting.

THE TICKET (SFCC-731, "pdp/gallery", status Code Review, assignee Tim Lavelle) — full Acceptance Criteria, verbatim, THIS is the authoritative scope document (the ticket's free-text description still says "the gallery overlay is a separate component and out of scope for this story" but that sentence is STALE — the AC list below was authored by the same reporter (Jasmijn Tsang) later the same day and is the more specific, more recent, active field. Do not flag "overlay is out of scope" as a violation; it isn't):

Default state — desktop layout
1. 3 media items → 3 full-width stacked + View Gallery button
2. 4 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery button
3. 5 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery +1 button
4. 6 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery button
5. 7+ media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery +X button (X = total minus 6)
6. Video items slot into the layout based on their position in the media array and are not treated differently to photo items for layout purposes.

showGalleryButton prop
7. Given showGalleryButton is false, then no View Gallery button renders regardless of media count.
8. Given showGalleryButton is true, then the View Gallery button renders per the layout thresholds above and is visible and tappable.

Default state — mobile
9. Given the component renders on mobile, then all media items display in a swipeable single-image carousel with a dot indicator bar regardless of media count.
10. Given a shopper swipes, then the active dot indicator updates to reflect the current position.
11. Given showGalleryButton is true on mobile, then the View Gallery button is visible and tappable.

Expanded state — overlay shell
12. Given the View Gallery button is activated, then the gallery opens full-screen taking over the entire viewport.
13. Given the gallery is open, then clicking the close icon dismisses the overlay and returns the shopper to their previous scroll position on the PDP.

Expanded state — gallery header (desktop)
14. Given the gallery is open on desktop, then a sticky header is visible at the top of the overlay containing: product name, active colour name, close icon, and model avatar thumbnails.
15. Given the product has multiple colour variants, then the header includes a colour selector.
16. Given a shopper clicks a model avatar thumbnail, then the gallery scrolls to the corresponding image set for that model.

Expanded state — gallery header (mobile)
17. Given the gallery is open on mobile, then a sticky header is visible containing: product name, close icon, and colour selector. Model avatar thumbnails are not shown on mobile.

Expanded state — image content
18. Given the gallery is open, then the full media array renders as a vertically scrollable stack of full-width media items.
19. Given the gallery renders, then images are served in an optimised format at the appropriate resolution per breakpoint.

Empty & error states
20. Given no media items exist for the product, then the component does not render and no broken layout is shown.
21. Given an image fails to load, then the surrounding layout is maintained without a broken image rendering.

Accessibility
22. Given the gallery overlay opens, then focus moves into it and is trapped within until closed.
23. Given the gallery overlay closes, then focus returns to the View Gallery button that triggered it.
24. The overlay has role=dialog and an appropriate aria-label.
25. The component meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

NOTE: AC 16 (model avatar thumbnails that scroll the gallery to a specific model's image set) depends on multi-model image-set data — check whether this PR actually implements AC 16, stubs it, or silently omits it; the PR's own commit messages never mention "model avatar thumbnails" at all, only a colour-swatch row in the overlay header. This looks like a real gap worth confirming.

FILES CHANGED (34 total, +3281/-475) — new: zimmMediaTile/* (atom), zimmProductGallery/* (organism), zimmGalleryOverlay/* (organism), zimmProductGallery/getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts, product-view/mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts, utils/buildDisImageSrc.ts. Modified: product-view/index.tsx, product-detail/index.tsx, pageContainer/index.tsx, zimmButton/index.tsx + .css.ts, zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx + .css.ts, zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx + .css.ts, theme/components/index.ts, theme/globalStyles.ts, plus registry files (.claude/registry/*.md — auto-generated, ignore).

ALREADY-FIXED CodeRabbit findings from this PR's own history — do not re-report these as new, but you MAY spot-check that the fix is actually correct/complete if you have reason to doubt it:
- MediaTile's image-error state now tracks the failed *source* (not a boolean), so a variation swap that replaces a failed image with a new valid one at the same list index recovers instead of staying stuck on the fallback.
- selectedIndex is clamped (render-time + effect) when a variation swap shrinks the media array, so it can't go out of bounds.
- COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID/SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID deduped to one shared constant, exported from product-view and imported into product-detail.
- Gallery z-index stacking levels named instead of magic numbers.
- A stale "Hidden below `xl`" comment on desktopColumn (leftover from an earlier xl→lg breakpoint fix) was corrected.
- A responsive-image-sources test now asserts sources.length > 0 first (previously could pass having asserted on zero elements).

STILL-OPEN CodeRabbit "nitpick" classifications (CodeRabbit itself called these low-severity/optional; independently verify whether that classification is right, don't just trust the label) — one of your reviewers should check these specifically:
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmMediaTile/index.tsx ~lines 71-103: the photo-kind and video-kind branches allegedly duplicate an identical AspectRatio+fallback+Image block, differing only in trailing video controls. Confirm the duplication is real and assess actual maintenance risk (is drift between the two branches actually likely/costly, or is this genuinely trivial).
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx ~line 193: `offeredColourCount` allegedly re-implements (duplicates) the same imageUrl/orderable filter that ZimmColourSwatchGroup applies internally to gate which swatches count as "offered" — meaning if the group's gating logic changes, this duplicate silently drifts out of sync. Confirm this duplication is real and whether it's a genuine correctness risk (e.g. could the overlay currently show a wrong "Also available in N colours" count in some real state) or just theoretical.

MY OWN ALREADY-CONFIRMED FINDING (do not re-investigate, just be aware): the PR branch currently has a REAL merge conflict against the current tip of develop in zimmButton/index.tsx — an already-merged, unrelated PR (SFCC-92, PDP size selection/add-to-bag) independently added an `ariaDisabled`/`ariaDescribedBy` pair to the same ZimmButton component (for accessible disabled-appearance-but-focusable buttons) that this PR's branch does not have; meanwhile this PR adds its own `sx` passthrough prop to the same component, in the same destructured-props line and same JSX prop-spread locations. Both features are legitimate and non-conflicting in intent, but git cannot auto-merge them — whoever resolves this must manually keep BOTH ariaDisabled/ariaDescribedBy (from develop) AND sx (from this PR) or silently regress the SFCC-92 accessibility fix. This is not something for you to fix or re-verify — just don't be confused if the checked-out head branch's zimmButton looks like it's missing ariaDisabled/ariaDescribedBy; that's expected, it's develop's addition, not something missing from this PR.

ANGLES TO COVER (dispatch your own sub-agents on distinct but overlapping briefs, per your normal approach):
1. Correctness & regression — getDesktopLayoutCounts.ts's logic against AC 1-6 exactly (all 5 count cases + boundaries), mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts's mapping correctness, MediaTile/selectedIndex edge cases beyond what's already fixed, AC 16's model-avatar-thumbnail gap noted above, AC 9/10 (mobile carousel + dot sync), AC 20 (empty media = no render).
2. Conventions, structure, and tier ownership — check against .claude/rules/conventions.md, components.md, typescript.md, css.md, overrideStyling.md (all loaded in this repo's CLAUDE.md context already, read them directly at their paths under .claude/rules/ in the worktree if you need the full text). Specifically: is zimmButton's new `sx` prop genuinely additive/backward-compatible for every other existing caller (grep all ZimmButton call sites)? Does the new sx-based `galleryButton` recipe part in zimmProductGallery.css.ts respect "one canonical styling surface per component" (overrideStyling.md)? Is JSDoc present on every exported hook/shared component per components.md? Does every new component have a *.stories.tsx and appropriate *.test.ts/tsx per testing.md's coverage expectations?
3. Contract fidelity — product-view/index.tsx now imports ZimmProductGallery in place of base ImageGallery for imageSize="md" while imageSize="sm" callers keep the base component; verify this split is actually correctly gated in the code (not just claimed) and that no imageSize="sm" caller (product-view-modal quick-view/bundle, bonus-product-view-modal) accidentally got the new gallery. Also verify ZimmColourSwatchGroup/ZimmColourSwatch's new circle variant doesn't break its existing square-variant callers (check all current call sites).
4. Failure modes & security — image error handling (already partly covered), focus-trap dialog correctness for ZimmGalleryOverlay (AC 22-24 — does it use a real focus trap, e.g. Chakra Modal/FocusLock, or hand-rolled and leaky?), buildDisImageSrc.ts's URL templating (any injection risk from unescaped product/variant identifiers, any case where a malformed input produces a broken or unsafe URL), video-as-positional-slot-only handling (does anything assume a video URL is always present in a way that would throw when video isn't wired up yet, consistent with SFCC-188 being blocked).
5. Token/styling strategy — spot-check the "acknowledged exception" raw values noted above for whether a real --zimm-* token already exists that should have been used instead of a new hardcoded value with a comment (check overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts, sizes.ts, zimmTokens.ts for anything matching 218px/45rem/6.375rem/etc. before concluding a token is genuinely missing).

For every finding, report: file:line, one-sentence defect statement, concrete failure scenario (what input/state causes what wrong output), and your confidence. Do not fix anything — findings only. Report back with your full findings list; I will verify them myself before deciding what's real.

1	/**
2	 * SFCC-731 AC 19 — wraps a raw SFCC product-image URL into the templated "dynamic src" format
3	 * base SFCC's `getResponsivePictureAttributes`/`DynamicImage` expect (see
4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/responsive-image.js`'s own `getSrc` doc comment):
5	 * a `[...]` segment containing a `{width}` placeholder that gets swapped in per breakpoint via
6	 * SFCC's Dynamic Imaging Service query params (`sw` = scale width, `q` = quality).
7	 *
8	 * Deliberately does not build the `<picture>`/`srcSet` logic itself — that already exists in
9	 * `DynamicImage` and shouldn't be duplicated. This is only the one SFCC-specific piece missing
10	 * from that generic utility: the actual DIS query string for a given image URL.
11	 *
12	 * `data:`/`blob:` URLs are returned unchanged, with no template wrapper — DIS server-side
13	 * resizing is meaningless for a URL that already *is* the image bytes (there's no server to ask),
14	 * and appending a query-string-shaped suffix to a base64 payload corrupts it outright (the
15	 * browser fails to decode it, `net::ERR_INVALID_URL`) rather than merely doing nothing useful.
16	 *
17	 * @param url - Raw SFCC image URL (`disBaseLink` or `link`), with or without existing query params.
18	 * @param quality - DIS `q` param (0-100). Defaults to 80 — user-confirmed as the right baseline
19	 *   for this brand's product photography (2026-09-05); 60, the base SFCC image-gallery
20	 *   component's own default, showed visible compression artifacts on fabric/detail shots.
21	 * @returns A templated src ready for `DynamicImage`'s `src` prop or base's `getSrc` helper.
22	 */
23	export const buildDisImageSrc = (url: string, quality = 80): string => {
24	  if (url.startsWith('data:') || url.startsWith('blob:')) return url;
25	  const separator = url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?';
26	  return `${url}[${separator}sw={width}&q=${quality}]`;
27	};
28	
29	/**
30	 * Resolves a `buildDisImageSrc` template to a single concrete URL at a given width — the
31	 * counterpart read side of the same `[...]`/`{width}` format, for a caller (e.g. a fixed-size
32	 * thumbnail) that needs one resolved src rather than `DynamicImage`'s full responsive
33	 * `<picture>`/`srcSet` treatment. A project-owned equivalent of base SFCC's own
34	 * `getSrc` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/responsive-image`), kept in-house so this
35	 * templated-src format has one owner instead of a cross-package import for two lines of regex
36	 * (CodeRabbit, PR #81).
37	 *
38	 * @param templatedSrc - Output of `buildDisImageSrc`, e.g. `https://x/img.jpg[?sw={width}&q=80]`.
39	 * @param width - Concrete pixel width to substitute for `{width}`.
40	 */
41	export const resolveDisImageSrc = (templatedSrc: string, width: number): string =>
42	  templatedSrc.replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g, '$1').replace(/\{[^}]+\}/g, String(width));
